claims.text: GDACS's event report for Kanlaon Volcano (GDACS event ID VO 1000152, event date 10 Oct 2026) rates the eruption an Orange alert, "likely to have a medium humanitarian impact based on the magnitude and the affected population's vulnerability," estimating about 870,000 people within 30km of the volcano and about 10,790,000 within 100km. Re-checked 4 November 2026: the report page is unchanged, still showing episode 1 as the latest with no updated exposure, casualty or displacement figures; dromic.dswd.gov.ph returned HTTP 503 and PHIVOLCS's own site (phivolcs.dost.gov.ph) carried no Kanlaon-specific bulletin, so no newer DSWD/PHIVOLCS report could be checked for this eruption.

claims.source_name: Department of Social Welfare and Development (Philippines)
claims.text: DSWD DROMIC Report #3 on the Kanlaon Volcano Eruption, as of 14 July 2026 6PM, recorded 18,856 families (62,785 persons) affected across 12 barangays in the Negros Island Region, with the volcano held at Alert Level 2 and communities within the 4km-radius Permanent Danger Zone instructed to remain evacuated.

claims.source_name: The Star (Malaysia), citing Philippine Office of Civil Defense
claims.text: News reports citing the Philippine Office of Civil Defense (OCD) said about 24,000 families (roughly 94,000 individuals) were affected by ashfall from the 10 October eruption, with 2,500 families (about 8,000 individuals) sheltering across 21 evacuation sites as of the 13 October briefing; PHIVOLCS reported continuing ash emissions on 11 and 12 October with the volcano held at Alert Level 2. These OCD-sourced figures have not been independently corroborated by an authoritative international source.

PHIVOLCS's Kanlaon bulletin dated 6 November 2026 maintains Alert Level 2 (increased unrest). Its 24-hour observation window ending at midnight on 6 November records 20 volcanic earthquakes; sulfur dioxide flux was 1,217 tonnes/day measured on 5 November. The bulletin prohibits entry into the 4km-radius Permanent Danger Zone and warns against aircraft flying close to the volcano. These are dated unrest observations and safety recommendations, not evidence of continuous eruption since October.

description: Mount Kanlaon on Negros Island, Philippines, erupted on 10 October 2026, prompting a GDACS Orange alert for potential humanitarian impact. PHIVOLCS's 6 November bulletin maintains Alert Level 2 for increased unrest and the 4km Permanent Danger Zone. GDACS's October event report estimates about 870,000 people within 30km and 10.79 million within 100km; these are exposure estimates, not counts of people displaced. October civil-defense displacement figures remain unverified in this record.

impact.summary: GDACS's October event report estimates about 870,000 people within 30km and 10.79 million within 100km. Verified casualty and displacement totals for the October eruption are not established in the cited evidence. PHIVOLCS recorded 20 volcanic earthquakes in its 6 November bulletin and SO2 flux of 1,217 tonnes/day measured on 5 November.
